title: Tune NCCL collectives and kernel scheduling for KV-cache continuous batching in tensor-parallel multi-GPU
author: Priya Singh
description: Motivation: reduce end-to-end token cost and tail latency for multi-GPU tensor-parallel workloads by improving overlap between NCCL collectives and CUDA kernel execution, and by making KV-cache continuous batching more scheduling-friendly. This PR applies a set of coordinated changes: (1) introduce prioritized NCCL streams and adjust stream ordering to avoid kernel-induced stalls, (2) add async progress hooks and reduce explicit stream synchronizations in the TP collective wrappers, (3) rework kernel launch order and introduce non-blocking kernel variants for attention/softmax to allow better overlap with communication, and (4) change KV-cache continuous-batching scheduling so cached prefixes are reused across microbatches while avoiding blocking synchronization points.

d4e5f6g: switch TP collectives to non-blocking launches and add async progress path
h7i8j9k: kernel changes: non-blocking attention kernel variant + reduce device-side atomic contention
l1m2n3o: update kvcache scheduler to avoid full-device syncs and reuse cached KV across microbatches
p4q5r6s: add multi-GPU benchmark harness updates + perf dashboards
t7u8v9w: tests and docs: perf notes and tuning guide
release_notes: Performance: Improve multi-GPU throughput by ~18% and reduce p99 latency by ~12% on 8-GPU TP configs. Reliability: reduce NCCL stalls caused by kernel syncs; KV-cache continuous batching now reuses prefix caches without global syncs. Ops: added knobs for NCCL stream priorities and an opt-in async-progress path.
benchmarks_summary: 8-GPU ResNet-like TP throughput +18% (median), p99 latency -12%; small regression (<2%) on single-GPU microbenchmarks. Stress tests show no deadlocks across 72h runs with mixed sequence lengths.
review_conversation: Alex Kim (reviewer): Can you add a short note about the safety of the async-progress path on older drivers?
Priya Singh (author): Added a runtime guard and a CI job targeting CUDA 11.4 / NCCL 2.10 to exercise the fallback path; documented in docs/perf/tp-nccl-tuning.md
Jorge Ramirez (reviewer): The non-blocking attention kernel looks good but please include a microbench that isolates attention kernel latency to ensure no regressions.
Priya Singh (author): Added tests/integration/tp_kvcache_overlap_test.py and updated the benchmark harness to record isolated kernel timings.
notes: This PR is the consolidation of several experimental branches that were validated internally on infra with mixed sequence lengths. Most of the complexity is confined to runtime/nccl and runtime/kvcache; callers can opt into the new behavior via config flags. The change was validated on A100 and H100 clusters; fallback paths remain for older driver/NCCL combos.
changelog_entry: tune: improve NCCL stream scheduling and KV-cache continuous batching overlap for tensor-parallel workloads (performance+stability)
test_plan: Unit + integration tests included. New CI job (gpu_nccl_tuning) runs full 8-GPU TP stress for 12h. Manual bench runs on A100/H100 cluster recorded and uploaded to perf dashboard. Smoke-tested in staging with Dedicated nodes.
impact_summary: Expected positive perf impact for multi-GPU TP serving. Operators should test upgrade path; config defaults keep current behavior unless opt-in flag is enabled. No user-visible API changes.
notes_for_release: Enable opt-in by setting runtime.tuning.enable_tp_nccL_overlaps = true. Follow docs/perf/tp-nccl-tuning.md for recommended knobs per cluster type.
